headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read files and Goose explicitly writes to the user filesystem with shared state via filesystem, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and supports MCP. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs from disk. The pathway is not proven by docs, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF agent_b reads files produced by agent_a without provenance checks, injected instructions can be followed.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, attacker-controlled content can traverse between them.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files.
Add a provenance header check before parsing any file.
Use read-only mounts for handoff artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and has broad network egress; gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and research reports. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can be exposed to either agent and then uploaded through their respective API-backed workflows. The shared-workspace plus outbound API pattern fits medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory containing secrets or private documents, leakage becomes plausible.
IF either agent forwards file contents to configured model or search APIs, those contents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets outside the shared workspace.
Use separate API keys per agent.
Block network egress for the research agent during sensitive tasks.
Redact files before either agent reads them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem read access, and Goose additionally has write_filesystem and modify_git_state while gpt-researcher can run browsers and spawn subprocesses. In a shared directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking, making destructive conflicts likely in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent commits or rewrites can conflict.
IF the orchestrator does not provide file locking, simultaneous writes can corrupt shared artifacts.
mitigations: Assign separate git branches per agent.
Disable concurrent writes to the same directory.
Add a lock file around git operations.
Run one agent read-only while the other writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can produce tool-driven outputs from code or filesystem state, and gpt-researcher is a planner/execution/publisher pipeline that can turn those outputs into reports. If gpt-researcher treats Goose's output as authoritative, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into published research or actions. The pairwise handoff is undocumented, so I choose the higher severity due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher ingests Goose-generated text without verification, false claims can propagate.
IF the publisher stage acts on unreviewed upstream output, downstream reports may embed errors.
mitigations: Require citation checks before publishing.
Insert a human review step between agents.
Mark Goose output as untrusted input.
Compare claims against source documents before actioning them.

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model provider keys and extension tokens, while gpt-researcher handles API keys and local documents/citations. If the pair is used on regulated or residency-sensitive data, the broad network/API surfaces can move data into third-party services without an explicit compliance boundary. No specific residency mismatch is documented, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace, it may be transmitted to external APIs.
IF the deployment requires residency controls, broad egress can violate them absent additional policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Use region-locked API endpoints where available.
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Add a data-class allowlist before ingestion.
